Belousova E.role: Co-author of the EXIST-1 and EXIST-2 everolimus trials in tuberous sclerosis complex.
Belousova E.sub: Moscow Research Institute of Pediatrics and Pediatric Surgery, Moscow, Russia
story: Elena Belousova is listed as a co-author of both large phase 3 trials of everolimus in tuberous sclerosis complex, EXIST-1 (brain tumors) and EXIST-2 (kidney tumors). In these people-based randomised trials everolimus, a drug that blocks mTOR, shrank the tumors much more often than placebo.

PubMed does not list her affiliation in these two records. A related paper from the same trial group lists her at the Moscow Research Institute of Pediatrics and Pediatric Surgery, and that is the affiliation used here.

highlights.BIS2013: Middle author of the EXIST-2 trial of everolimus for kidney angiomyolipomas.
highlights.FRA2013: Second author of the EXIST-1 trial of everolimus for brain tumors (SEGA).

Belousova E.lab_name: Moscow Research Institute of Pediatrics and Pediatric Surgery (Moscow, Russia)

Whittemore VH.role: Co-author of the EXIST-1 trial of everolimus for brain tumors in tuberous sclerosis complex.
Whittemore VH.sub: National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke, National Institutes of Health, Bethesda, MD, USA
story: Vicky H Whittemore is a co-author of EXIST-1, a phase 3 randomised trial in people with tuberous sclerosis complex. Everolimus, a drug that blocks mTOR, shrank brain tumors (SEGA) by at least half in 35% of patients, against none on placebo.

PubMed gives no affiliation in the trial record. A later paper that shares co-authors Franz and de Vries lists her at the National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke, so that is used here.
Whittemore VH.lab_name: National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke, National Institutes of Health (Bethesda, MD, USA)

Stitt TN.role: Co-author of two 2001 studies on Akt/mTOR signalling and muscle growth.
story: Trevor N Stitt is a co-author of two 2001 papers from the same group on how muscle cells grow. One, in rats, showed that Akt/mTOR signalling drives muscle growth and can prevent muscle wasting. The other, in cultured muscle fibres, showed that IGF-1 makes them larger through Akt, using both the mTOR and the GSK3 branches.
The 2001 records give only his initials. His full name and Regeneron affiliation come from a 2004 paper from the same group that shares several co-authors with both studies.

highlights.BOD2001: Middle author of the study on Akt/mTOR in muscle hypertrophy in rats.
highlights.ROM2001: Middle author of the study on IGF-1 signalling in cultured muscle fibres.

Pollizzi KN.role: First author of the study on mTORC1 and mTORC2 in CD8 T cells, and co-author of the study on helper T cells.
Pollizzi KN.sub: Sidney-Kimmel Comprehensive Cancer Research Center, Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine, Baltimore, MD, USA
story: Kristen N Pollizzi was first author of a mouse study that separated the jobs of the two mTOR complexes in CD8 T cells. Cells with constantly active mTORC1 became strong, short-lived effector cells. Cells lacking mTORC1 kept memory features but responded poorly on a second exposure. mTORC2 activity influenced memory.

She is also a co-author of a mouse study showing that mTORC1 and mTORC2 steer helper T cells toward different fates. PubMed gives no affiliation in these records. A 2016 paper from the same group lists her at Johns Hopkins, and that is used here.

highlights.POL2015: First author of the study on mTORC1 and mTORC2 in CD8 T cell differentiation.
highlights.DEL2011: Co-author of the study on mTORC1 and mTORC2 in helper T cell differentiation.

Pollizzi KN.lab_name: Department of Oncology, Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine (Baltimore, MD, USA)

Waickman AT.role: Co-author of the studies on mTOR complexes in CD8 and helper T cells.
Waickman AT.sub: Sidney-Kimmel Comprehensive Cancer Research Center, Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine, Baltimore, MD, USA
story: Adam T Waickman is a co-author of two mouse studies on how the two mTOR complexes shape T cells. One showed that mTORC1 and mTORC2 play different roles in CD8 effector and memory cells. The other showed that they steer helper T cells toward different fates.
PubMed gives no affiliation in these records. A 2016 paper from the same group lists him at Johns Hopkins, and that is used here.

highlights.POL2015: Fifth author of the CD8 T cell study.
highlights.DEL2011: Third author of the helper T cell study.

Waickman AT.lab_name: Department of Oncology, Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine (Baltimore, MD, USA)

Ikenoue T.role: Co-author of the study that identified Sin1 as an essential part of mTORC2.
Ikenoue T.sub: Life Sciences Institute, University of Michigan, Ann Arbor, MI, USA
story: Tsuneo Ikenoue is a co-author of a cell study that identified Sin1 as an essential part of the mTORC2 complex. Without Sin1 the complex did not form properly and could not add the phosphate group to Akt that it normally adds.
PubMed gives no affiliation in that record. A 2008 paper that shares co-authors Inoki and Guan lists him at the Life Sciences Institute, University of Michigan, and that is used here.

highlights.YAN2006: Co-author of the Sin1 and mTORC2 study.

Ikenoue T.lab_name: Life Sciences Institute, University of Michigan (Ann Arbor, MI, USA)
